top_papers.title: Lineage-specific imprinting and evolution of the zinc-finger gene ZIM2.
top_papers.abstract: We have carried out an in-depth comparative analysis of a 100-kb genomic interval containing two imprinted genes, PEG3 and ZIM2, using sequences derived from human, mouse, and cow. In all three mammals, ZIM2 is located at a similar genomic distance and in the same orientation relative to PEG3, indicating the basic structural conservation of this imprinted locus. However, several lineage-specific changes have occurred that affect the exon structure and imprinting status of ZIM2. Human ZIM2 and PEG3 share a set of 5' exons and a common promoter, and both genes are paternally expressed. In contrast, mouse and cow Zim2 genes do not share 5' exons with Peg3, and Zim2 employs a separate downstream promoter in both species. The imprinting status of Zim2 is also not conserved among mammals; mouse Zim2 is expressed biallelically in testis but predominantly from the maternal allele in brain, while cow Zim2 is expressed biallelically in testis. The separate transcription of Zim2 and Peg3 and the change in promoter usage and imprinting status appear to have resulted from independent insertional events that have placed unrelated genes, Zim1 and Ast1, respectively, between Zim2 and Peg3 in mouse and cow. Our results suggest that PEG3 and ZIM2 represent the two original genes at this locus and that rearrangements have occurred independently in different mammalian lineages in recent evolutionary times. Our data also suggest that exon-sharing of human PEG3 and ZIM2 was not ancestral, but may represent a fusion event joining the two neighboring genes and bringing ZIM2 under paternal expression control. These observations are striking in light of the structural and functional conservation that typifies other imprinted domains and suggest that the PEG3/ZIM2 imprinted domain may have evolved in an unusual lineage-specific pattern.

top_papers.title: Exon sharing of a novel human zinc-finger gene, ZIM2, and paternally expressed gene 3 (PEG3).
top_papers.abstract: We have identified a novel human gene, ZIM2 (zinc-finger gene 2 from imprinted domain), located 25 kb downstream of PEG3 (paternally expressed gene 3). ZIM2 produces two different-size transcripts, 2.5 and 9.0 kb in length, with highest levels of expression in adult testis and modest levels in fetal kidney and brain. The 2.5-kb transcript of ZIM2 consists of 11 exons and encodes a Kruppel-type (C2H2) zinc-finger protein with a conserved Kruppel-associated box (KRAB) domain. Rapid amplification of cDNA ends and cDNA sequencing studies showed that ZIM2 and PEG3 transcripts share identical 5'-ends, composed of 7 small exons. Alternative splicing events connect these 7 exons either with the remaining 2 exons of PEG3 or with the remaining 4 exons of ZIM2. Interestingly, the third among the 7 shared exons exhibits sequence similarity to leucine-rich domains that are found at the N-terminal region of a subset of KRAB-containing zinc-finger genes. Sequencing of the 5'-termini of both transcripts indicates that ZIM2 and PEG3 share identical transcription start sites and may also share upstream regulatory elements, although the two genes show distinct patterns of tissue-specific expression.

top_papers.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of transient neonatal diabetes type 1 patients with mutations in ZFP57.
top_papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus 1 (TNDM1) is a rare imprinting disorder characterized by intrautering growth retardation and diabetes mellitus usually presenting within the first six weeks of life and resolves by the age of 18 months. However, patients have an increased risk of developing diabetes mellitus type 2 later in life. Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus 1 is caused by overexpression of the maternally imprinted genes PLAGL1 and HYMAI on chromosome 6q24. One of the mechanisms leading to overexpression of the locus is hypomethylation of the maternal allele of PLAGL1 and HYMAI. A subset of patients with maternal hypomethylation at PLAGL1 have hypomethylation at additional imprinted loci throughout the genome, including GRB10, ZIM2 (PEG3), MEST (PEG1), KCNQ1OT1 and NESPAS (GNAS-AS1). About half of the TNDM1 patients carry mutations in ZFP57, a transcription factor involved in establishment and maintenance of methylation of imprinted loci. Our objective was to investigate whether additional regions are aberrantly methylated in ZFP57 mutation carriers. METHODS: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis was performed on four individuals with homozygous or compound heterozygous ZFP57 mutations, three relatives with heterozygous ZFP57 mutations and five controls. Methylation status of selected regions showing aberrant methylation in the patients was verified using bisulfite-sequencing. RESULTS: We found large variability among the patients concerning the number and identity of the differentially methylated regions, but more than 60 regions were aberrantly methylated in two or more patients and a novel region within PPP1R13L was found to be hypomethylated in all the patients. The hypomethylated regions in common between the patients are enriched for the ZFP57 DNA binding motif. CONCLUSIONS: We have expanded the epimutational spectrum of TNDM1 associated with ZFP57 mutations and found one novel region within PPP1R13L which is hypomethylated in all TNDM1 patients included in this study. Functional studies of the locus might provide further insight into the etiology of the disease.
top_papers.key_finding: Reported hypomethylation at the ZIM2 imprinted locus among other imprinted genes in transient neonatal diabetes type 1 patients with ZFP57 mutations, implicating ZIM2 in imprinting defects.

top_papers.title: Identification of an evolutionarily conserved cis-regulatory element controlling the Peg3 imprinted domain.
top_papers.abstract: The mammalian Peg3 domain harbors more than 20 evolutionarily conserved regions (ECRs) that are spread over the 250-kb genomic interval. The majority of these ECRs are marked with two histone modifications, H3K4me1 and H3K27ac, suggesting potential roles as distant regulatory elements for the transcription of the nearby imprinted genes. In the current study, the chromatin conformation capture (3C) method was utilized to detect potential interactions of these ECRs with the imprinted genes. According to the results, one region, ECR18, located 200-kb upstream of Peg3 interacts with the two promoter regions of Peg3 and Zim2. The observed interaction is most prominent in brain, but was also detected in testis. Histone modification and DNA methylation on ECR18 show no allele bias, implying that this region is likely functional on both alleles. In vitro assays also reveal ECR18 as a potential enhancer or repressor for the promoter of Peg3. Overall, these results indicate that the promoters of several imprinted genes in the Peg3 domain interact with one evolutionarily conserved region, ECR18, and further suggest that ECR18 may play key roles in the transcription and imprinting control of the Peg3 domain as a distant regulatory element.

top_papers.title: Sterol O-acyltransferase 1 (SOAT1, ACAT) is a novel target of steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1, NR5A1, Ad4BP) in the human adrenal.
top_papers.abstract: CONTEXT: Steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1, NR5A1, Ad4BP) is a master regulator of adrenal development and steroidogenesis. Defects in several known targets of SF-1 can cause adrenal disorders in humans. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to identify novel targets of SF-1 in the human adrenal. These factors could be important regulators of adrenal development and steroidogenesis and potential candidates for adrenal dysfunction. DESIGN: A gene discovery strategy was developed based on bidirectional manipulation of SF-1. Overexpression or knockdown of SF-1 in NCI-H295R human adrenocortical cells was used to identify a subset of positively-regulated SF-1 targets. RESULTS: This approach identified well-established SF-1 target genes (STAR, CYP11A) and several novel genes (VSNL1, ZIM2, PEG3, SOAT1, and MTSS1). Given its role in cholesterol metabolism, sterol O-acyltransferase 1 (SOAT1, previously referred to as acyl-Coenzyme A:cholesterol acyltransferase 1, ACAT) was studied further and found to be expressed in the developing human fetal adrenal cortex. We hypothesized that impaired SOAT1 activity could result in adrenal insufficiency through reduced cholesteryl ester reserves or through toxic destruction of the adrenal cells during development. Therefore, mutational analysis of SOAT1 in a cohort of 43 patients with unexplained adrenal insufficiency was performed but failed to reveal significant coding sequence changes. CONCLUSIONS: Our reverse discovery approach led to the identification of novel SF-1 targets and defined SOAT1 as an important factor in human adrenal steroidogenesis. SF-1-dependent up-regulation of SOAT1 may be important for maintaining readily-releasable cholesterol reserves needed for active steroidogenesis and during episodes of recurrent stress.
top_papers.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
top_papers.key_finding: Identified ZIM2 as a novel target gene positively regulated by steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1) in human adrenal cells, suggesting a role in adrenal development and steroidogenesis.

top_papers.title: A comparative genomic database of skeletogenesis genes: from fish to mammals.
top_papers.abstract: Skeletogenesis is a complex process that requires a rigorous control at multiple levels during osteogenesis, such as signaling pathways and transcription factors. The skeleton among vertebrates is a highly conserved organ system, but teleost fish and mammals have evolved unique traits or have lost particular skeletal elements in each lineage. In present study, we constructed a skeletogenesis database containing 4101, 3715, 2996, 3300, 3719 and 3737 genes in Danio rerio, Oryzias latipes, Gallus gallus, Xenopus tropicalis, Mus musculus and Homo sapiens genome, respectively. Then, we found over 55% of the genes are conserved in the six species. Notably, there are 181 specific-genes in the human genome without orthologues in the other five genomes, such as the ZNF family (ZNF100, ZNF101, ZNF14, CALML6, CCL4L2, ZIM2, HSPA6, etc); and 31 genes are identified explicitly in fish species, which are mainly involved in TGF-beta, Wnt, MAPK, Calcium signaling pathways, such as bmp16, bmpr2a, eif4e1c, wnt2ba, etc. Particularly, there are 20 zebrafish-specific genes (calm3a, si:dkey-25li10, drd1a, drd7, etc) and one medaka-specific gene (c-myc17) that may alter skeletogenesis formation in the corresponding species. The database provides the new systematic genomic insights into skeletal development from teleosts to mammals, which may help to explain some of the complexities of skeletal phenotypes among different vertebrates and provide a reference for the treatment of skeletal diseases as well as for applications in the aquaculture industry.
top_papers.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
top_papers.key_finding: Included ZIM2 among human-specific genes in a comparative genomic database related to skeletogenesis, highlighting its potential unique role in human skeletal formation.

top_papers.title: Pancreatic cancer genomes reveal aberrations in axon guidance pathway genes.
top_papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy with few effective therapies. We performed exome sequencing and copy number analysis to define genomic aberrations in a prospectively accrued clinical cohort (n = 142) of early (stage I and II) sporadic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Detailed analysis of 99 informative tumours identified substantial heterogeneity with 2,016 non-silent mutations and 1,628 copy-number variations. We define 16 significantly mutated genes, reaffirming known mutations (KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A, SMAD4, MLL3, TGFBR2, ARID1A and SF3B1), and uncover novel mutated genes including additional genes involved in chromatin modification (EPC1 and ARID2), DNA damage repair (ATM) and other mechanisms (ZIM2, MAP2K4, NALCN, SLC16A4 and MAGEA6). Integrative analysis with in vitro functional data and animal models provided supportive evidence for potential roles for these genetic aberrations in carcinogenesis. Pathway-based analysis of recurrently mutated genes recapitulated clustering in core signalling pathways in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and identified new mutated genes in each pathway. We also identified frequent and diverse somatic aberrations in genes described traditionally as embryonic regulators of axon guidance, particularly SLIT/ROBO signalling, which was also evident in murine Sleeping Beauty transposon-mediated somatic mutagenesis models of pancreatic cancer, providing further supportive evidence for the potential involvement of axon guidance genes in pancreatic carcinogenesis.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified ZIM2 as one of the novel mutated genes in pancreatic cancer genomes, suggesting possible involvement in carcinogenesis pathways.

top_papers.title: Identification of an antisense transcript to ZIM2 in the primate lineage.
top_papers.abstract: In this study, we identified an antisense transcript to ZIM2 (zinc finger imprinted gene 2) in the human, called ZIM2as. Sequence analysis of the 110 kb region spanned by this transcript revealed a cluster of tandemly repeated sequence in the human, orangutan, and chimpanzee as well as a loss of approximately 70 kb from the corresponding region in the rhesus. The homologous region in most mammals contains a cluster of olfactory receptor (OLFR) genes, but this gene cluster has been lost from the primate lineage. Expression analyses confirmed that ZIM2as is expressed in the human brain and testis. Two CpG islands near the promoter region of ZIM2as showed different methylation patterns in these three species. The CpG island distal to ZIM2as showed an allele-specific DNA methylation pattern in the human testis, while the CpG island proximal to the ZIM2as promoter showed a mosaic methylation pattern in the chimpanzee. The methylation status of several nearby zinc finger genes was unchanged among the primates tested. Overall, this study reports the presence of a previously unreported primate-specific antisense transcript in the PEG3 imprinted domain, suggesting that the formation of this transcript may coincide with the loss of the OLFR cluster.

top_papers.title: Epigenetic footprints: Investigating placental DNA methylation in the context of prenatal exposure to phenols and phthalates.
top_papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) such as phthalates and phenols can affect placental functioning and fetal health, potentially via epigenetic modifications. We investigated the associations between pregnancy exposure to synthetic phenols and phthalates estimated from repeated urine sampling and genome wide placental DNA methylation. METHODS: The study is based on 387 women with placental DNA methylation assessed with Infinium MethylationEPIC arrays and with 7 phenols, 13 phthalates, and two non-phthalate plasticizer metabolites measured in pools of urine samples collected twice during pregnancy. We conducted an exploratory analysis on individual CpGs (EWAS) and differentially methylated regions (DMRs) as well as a candidate analysis focusing on 20 previously identified CpGs. Sex-stratified analyses were also performed. RESULTS: In the exploratory analysis, when both sexes were studied together no association was observed in the EWAS. In the sex-stratified analysis, 114 individual CpGs (68 in males, 46 in females) were differentially methylated, encompassing 74 genes (36 for males and 38 for females). We additionally identified 28 DMRs in the entire cohort, 40 for females and 42 for males. Associations were mostly positive (for DMRs: 93% positive associations in the entire cohort, 60% in the sex-stratified analysis), with the exception of several associations for bisphenols and DINCH metabolites that were negative. Biomarkers associated with most DMRs were parabens, DEHP, and DiNP metabolite concentrations. Some DMRs encompassed imprinted genes including APC (associated with parabens and DiNP metabolites), GNAS (bisphenols), ZIM2;PEG3;MIMT1 (parabens, monoethyl phthalate), and SGCE;PEG10 (parabens, DINCH metabolites). Terms related to adiposity, lipid and glucose metabolism, and cardiovascular function were among the enriched phenotypes associated with differentially methylated CpGs. The candidate analysis identified one CpG mapping to imprinted LGALS8 gene, negatively associated with ethylparaben. CONCLUSIONS: By combining improved exposure assessment and extensive placental epigenome coverage, we identified several novel genes associated with the exposure, possibly in a sex-specific manner.
top_papers.key_finding: ZIM2 was discussed in the context of placental DNA methylation associated with prenatal exposure to phenols and phthalates; no information is available about ZIM2-AS1, necroptosis, glioma, or prognostic models in the source data.

top_papers.title: Paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 19 in a pair of monochorionic diamniotic twins with dysmorphic features and developmental delay.
top_papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: We report here clinical, cytogenetic and molecular data for a pair of monochorionic diamniotic twins with paternal isodisomy for chromosome 19. Both twins presented with dysmorphic features and global developmental delay. This represents, to our knowledge, the first individual human case of paternal uniparental disomy for chromosome 19 (UPD19). METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing, together with conventional karyotype and SNP array analysis were performed along with genome-wide DNA methylation array for delineation of the underlying molecular defects. RESULTS: Conventional karyotyping on amniocytes and lymphocytes showed normal karyotypes for both twins. Whole-exome sequencing did not identify any pathogenic sequence variants but >5000 homozygous exonic variants on chromosome 19, suggestive of UPD19. SNP arrays on blood and buccal DNA both showed paternal isodisomy for chromosome 19. Losses of imprinting for known imprinted genes on chromosome 19 were identified, including  CONCLUSION: Imprinting defects are the most likely cause for the dysmorphism and developmental delay in this first report of monozygotic twins with UPD19. However, epigenotype-phenotype correlation will require identification of additional individuals with UPD19 and further molecular analysis.

top_papers.key_finding: Overexpression of P-Rex1 leads to aberrant neuronal polarity and psychosis-related behaviors, implicating P-Rex1 in neuronal development and higher brain functions through effects on cytoskeletal reorganization and cell motility.

top_papers.title: Identification of P-Rex1 as an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrogenic target for pulmonary fibrosis.
top_papers.key_finding: P-Rex1 acts as an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrogenic target in pulmonary fibrosis, with genetic deletion of P-Rex1 reducing lung fibroblast migration, Rac1 activation, and TGFβ-1 signaling, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression.

top_papers.title: Structural and Biochemical Characterization of the Catalytic Core of the Metastatic Factor P-Rex1 and Its Regulation by PtdIns(3,4,5)P3.
top_papers.key_finding: This study provides structural and biochemical characterization of the catalytic core of P-Rex1 and reveals that PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 binding to the PH domain is required for P-Rex1 activity, offering insights into its regulation and potential cancer therapeutic targeting.

top_papers.title: Astrocytic TCF7L2 Impacts Brain Osmoregulation and Restricts Neuronal Excitability.
top_papers.key_finding: Astrocytic TCF7L2 is crucial for coordinating ion and amino acid transport, maintaining extracellular homeostasis, and supporting neuronal function by regulating genes related to amino acid and ion transport and membrane potential.

top_papers.title: TCF7l2 Regulates Fatty Acid Chain Elongase HACD3 during Lipid-Induced Stress.
top_papers.key_finding: TCF7L2 regulates the fatty acid chain elongase HACD3 during lipid-induced stress, linking TCF7L2 transcriptional activity to metabolic homeostasis and type 2 diabetes-related pathways.

top_papers.title: Targeting the NOTCH2/ADAM10/TCF7L2 Axis-Mediated Transcriptional Regulation of Wnt Pathway Suppresses Tumor Growth and Enhances Chemosensitivity in Colorectal Cancer.
top_papers.key_finding: NOTCH2/ADAM10 axis mediates transcriptional regulation of TCF7L2 and Wnt target genes in colorectal cancer, and targeting this pathway suppresses tumor growth and enhances chemosensitivity.

top_papers.title: Tcf4 regulates secretory cell fate decisions in the small intestine and colon tumors: insights from transcriptomic, histological, and microbiome analyses.
top_papers.key_finding: Tcf4 (TCF7L2) regulates secretory cell fate decisions in the small intestine and colon tumors, influencing Paneth cell differentiation and antimicrobial peptide expression, highlighting its role in intestinal biology and tumorigenesis.

top_papers.title: De novo variants in TCF7L2 are associated with a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder.
top_papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
top_papers.key_finding: De novo variants in TCF7L2 are associated with a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delays, mild intellectual disability, and neuropsychiatric comorbidities, implicating TCF7L2 in neurodevelopment.

top_papers.title: N-Acetylglucosamine Kinase-Small Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein Polypeptide N Interaction Promotes Axodendritic Branching in Neurons via Dynein-Mediated Microtubule Transport.
top_papers.key_finding: NAGK and SNRPN interaction promotes axodendritic branching and neuronal complexity via dynein-mediated microtubule transport, and their overexpression rescues impaired neurodevelopment in SNRPN depletion models of Prader-Willi syndrome.

top_papers.title: Abnormal DNA methylation in pluripotent stem cells from a patient with Prader-Willi syndrome results in neuronal differentiation defects.
top_papers.key_finding: Abnormal methylation of SNRPN in iPS cells from a Prader-Willi syndrome patient leads to defective neuronal differentiation, indicating methylation-regulated SNRPN expression impacts neurodevelopment.

top_papers.title: Small Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein Polypeptide N Accelerates Malignant Progression and Poor Prognosis in Colorectal Cancer Transcriptionally Regulated by E2F8.
top_papers.key_finding: SNRPN is highly expressed in colorectal cancer tissues and correlates with tumor size, neural invasion, metastasis, and poor patient survival, indicating its role in malignant progression and as a prognostic biomarker.

top_papers.title: TET3 prevents terminal differentiation of adult NSCs by a non-catalytic action at Snrpn.
top_papers.key_finding: TET3 binds to the paternal allele of Snrpn to repress its transcription, preventing premature differentiation of adult neural stem cells into astrocytes, thus maintaining the NSC pool in the adult brain.

top_papers.title: The autism-related gene SNRPN regulates cortical and spine development via controlling nuclear receptor Nr4a1.
top_papers.key_finding: SNRPN regulates cortical and spine development by controlling nuclear receptor Nr4a1, with both overexpression and knockdown impairing neurite outgrowth and neuron migration, highlighting its critical role in neural development.

top_papers.title: Diverse changes in myelin protein expression in rat brain after perinatal methadone exposure.
top_papers.key_finding: Perinatal methadone exposure decreases CNP protein expression in multiple brain regions, indicating direct effects on myelin protein expression and oligodendrocyte function.

top_papers.title: Epigenomic signature of adrenoleukodystrophy predicts compromised oligodendrocyte differentiation.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified hypermethylation of the CNP gene among others, suggesting compromised oligodendrocyte differentiation in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, indicating a direct role of CNP gene epigenomic changes in disease pathology.

top_papers.title: Brain and Serum Membrane Vesicle (Exosome) Profiles in Experimental Alcohol-Related Brain Degeneration: Forging the Path to Non-Invasive Liquid Biopsy Diagnostics.
top_papers.key_finding: Ethanol exposure decreases expression of CNPase, a marker of oligodendrocytes, in brain tissue and serum exosomes, linking CNP protein to alcohol-related brain degeneration.

top_papers.title: Cocaine Administration and Its Abstinence Conditions Modulate Neuroglia.
top_papers.key_finding: CNP expression is decreased in the hippocampus after cocaine self-administration, implicating CNP in oligodendrocyte and myelin-related changes in addiction.

top_papers.title: Paracrine and endocrine pathways of natriuretic peptides assessed by ligand-receptor mapping in the Japanese eel brain.
top_papers.key_finding: Describes multiple CNP paralogues and their receptor interactions in Japanese eel brain, providing evolutionary and functional insights into CNP gene family in teleosts.

top_papers.title: Human glycogenins maintain glucose homeostasis by regulating glycogen metabolism.
top_papers.key_finding: This study reveals distinct physiological roles of human glycogenins GYG1 and GYG2 in glycogen synthesis, showing that GYG2 acts as a suppressor of glycogen formation and together with GYG1 regulates glycogen synthase activity and glucose homeostasis.

top_papers.title: Transcriptome-wide analysis reveals GYG2 as a mitochondria-related aging biomarker in human subcutaneous adipose tissue.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified GYG2 as a novel mitochondria-related aging biomarker in human subcutaneous adipose tissue, linking its expression to mitochondrial function and brown/beige adipocytes, with PPARG as a transcriptional regulator.

top_papers.title: Glycogen Synthesis in Glycogenin 1-Deficient Patients: A Role for Glycogenin 2 in Muscle.
top_papers.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
top_papers.key_finding: Demonstrated that in glycogenin 1-deficient patients, glycogenin 2 is expressed in muscle and may compensate for glycogen synthesis, suggesting an alternative pathway for glycogen buildup involving GYG2.

top_papers.title: A hemizygous GYG2 mutation and Leigh syndrome: a possible link?
top_papers.key_finding: Identified a hemizygous missense mutation in GYG2 in male siblings with Leigh syndrome, demonstrating that the mutation destabilizes the protein structure and abolishes its self-glucosylation activity, implicating GYG2 malfunction in disease.

top_papers.title: Functional analysis and verification of GYG2 in oncolytic virus-infected glioma.
top_papers.key_finding: Shows that GYG2 expression is downregulated after oncolytic virus infection in glioma cells and that high GYG2 expression correlates with poor prognosis, implicating GYG2 in glioma cell growth and apoptosis regulation.

top_papers.title: A-kinase anchoring protein 17 A promotes hypoxic adaptation and tumor growth by augmenting HIF1α protein synthesis.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A promotes hypoxic adaptation and tumor growth by augmenting HIF1α protein synthesis through a PKA-independent mechanism; depletion reduces HIF1α and tumor proliferation, showing AKAP17A's pivotal regulatory role in hypoxia and oncogenesis.

top_papers.title: Proteomic analysis reveals CAAP1 negatively correlates with platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A interacts with the splicing factor CAAP1 and is implicated in mRNA splicing pathways affecting platinum sensitivity in ovarian cancer cells, suggesting a role in chemotherapy response.

top_papers.title: The transcript expression levels of HNRNPM, HNRNPA0 and AKAP17A splicing factors may be predictively associated with ageing phenotypes in human peripheral blood.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A transcript levels in human peripheral blood are predictively associated with cognitive decline and some physical ageing phenotypes, indicating its potential role in ageing-related splicing regulation.

top_papers.title: Host Genetic and Gut Microbial Signatures in Familial Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A harbors rare, potentially deleterious variants transmitted in familial inflammatory bowel disease, indicating a possible genetic contribution to disease risk.

top_papers.title: Transcriptome profiling of fetal Klinefelter testis tissue reveals a possible involvement of long non-coding RNAs in gonocyte maturation.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A is upregulated in fetal Klinefelter syndrome testes, suggesting a possible involvement in gonocyte maturation and testicular development abnormalities.

top_papers.title: Vps34-orchestrated lipid signaling processes regulate the transitional heterogeneity and functional adaptation of effector regulatory T cells.
top_papers.key_finding: Genetic deletion of UVRAG in regulatory T cells demonstrates its role in effector Treg transitional heterogeneity and immune homeostasis, highlighting UVRAG's importance in immune regulation.

top_papers.title: Ubiquitination of UVRAG by SMURF1 promotes autophagosome maturation and inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma growth.
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG is ubiquitinated by SMURF1 which promotes autophagosome maturation and inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma growth; deubiquitination by ZRANB1 reverses this effect, revealing a regulatory mechanism of UVRAG in autophagy.

top_papers.title: Central role of autophagic UVRAG in melanogenesis and the suntan response.
top_papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG plays a central role in melanogenesis and the suntan response by stabilizing BLOC-1 complex and mediating cargo sorting to melanosomes; it acts as an effector of MITF and links UVRAG function to melanoma predisposition.

top_papers.title: miR-216b enhances the efficacy of vemurafenib by targeting Beclin-1, UVRAG and ATG5 in melanoma.
top_papers.key_finding: miR-216b targets UVRAG along with Beclin-1 and ATG5 to attenuate autophagy and overcome drug resistance in melanoma, highlighting UVRAG's role in autophagy-mediated cancer drug resistance.

top_papers.title: miR-183 regulates autophagy and apoptosis in colorectal cancer through targeting of UVRAG.
top_papers.key_finding: miR-183 targets UVRAG to inhibit autophagy and apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells; overexpression of UVRAG rescues autophagy and apoptosis, implicating UVRAG as a key regulator in cancer progression.

top_papers.title: DDR2-COL11A1 Transcriptional Coupling as a Candidate Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer: Integrative Transcriptomic and Deep Learning Validation.
top_papers.key_finding: DDR2-COL11A1 transcriptional coupling is significantly intensified in colorectal cancer progression, suggesting COL11A1 upregulation and its transcriptional coupling with DDR2 as a candidate therapeutic target.

top_papers.title: Lactate derived from macrophages drives skin dermal fibroblasts phenotypic remodeling via MCT1-primed histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation in hypertrophic scar.
top_papers.key_finding: COL11A1 is transcriptionally activated via histone lactylation in hypertrophic scar fibroblasts, forming a positive feedback loop with MCT1 that promotes fibrosis and scar formation.

top_papers.title: COL11A1 Inhibits Ferroptosis in Pancreatic Cancer by Regulating AKT/Beclin 1 Dependent Autophagy.
top_papers.key_finding: COL11A1 inhibits ferroptosis in pancreatic cancer cells by regulating AKT/Beclin 1-dependent autophagy, promoting cancer cell viability and chemoresistance.

top_papers.title: The FUS/COL11A1/ZEB1 Axis Contributes to the Development of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
top_papers.journal: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology
top_papers.key_finding: The FUS/COL11A1/ZEB1 axis promotes oral squamous cell carcinoma progression by regulating EMT, cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, with COL11A1 playing a critical mechanistic role.

top_papers.title: Unlocking cellular plasticity: enhancing human iPSC reprogramming through bromodomain inhibition and extracellular matrix gene expression regulation.
top_papers.key_finding: COL11A1 acts as a reprogramming barrier during human iPSC formation, and its knockdown increases reprogramming efficiency by reducing extracellular matrix gene expression and enhancing cellular plasticity.

top_papers.title: HDHD1, which is often deleted in X-linked ichthyosis, encodes a pseudouridine-5'-phosphatase.
top_papers.key_finding: This study identifies HDHD1 (alias of PUDP) as encoding a pseudouridine-5'-phosphatase enzyme, characterizing its enzymatic activity and confirming its molecular identity, thus directly elucidating the function of the PUDP gene.

top_papers.title: X chromosome dosage and the genetic impact across human tissues.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper analyzes X chromosome gene expression and methylation patterns across tissues, identifying genes with unexpected expression patterns; PUDP (HDHD1) as an X chromosomal gene may be implicated in these dosage effects, though PUDP is not the primary focus.

top_papers.title: No title
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions X-linked ichthyosis linked to deletions in Xp22.3 region potentially involving PUDP, but provides no detailed analysis or direct study of PUDP gene function or expression.

top_papers.title: Novel Microdeletion in the X Chromosome Leads to Kallmann Syndrome, Ichthyosis, Obesity, and Strabismus.
top_papers.key_finding: Reports a microdeletion in Xp22.3 region that may include PUDP gene, contributing to contiguous gene syndromes; however, PUDP is only mentioned as part of the deleted region without direct functional study.

top_papers.title: Genome-wide association analysis of treatment resistant schizophrenia for variant discovery and polygenic assessment.
top_papers.key_finding: No direct mention or study of PUDP gene; PUDP is not discussed in the context of schizophrenia genetics or treatment response.

top_papers.title: Alteration of colonic epithelial cell differentiation in mice deficient for glucosaminyl N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase 4.
top_papers.key_finding: Generated Ndst4 knockout mice and found that NDST4 deficiency alters colonic epithelial cell differentiation, increasing goblet cells and decreasing colonocytes, indicating a role in colonic epithelial homeostasis.

top_papers.title: NDST4 is a novel candidate tumor suppressor gene at chromosome 4q26 and its genetic loss predicts adverse prognosis in colorectal cancer.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified NDST4 as a novel candidate tumor suppressor gene at chromosome 4q26 with marked downregulation in colorectal cancer tumors and allelic loss predicting adverse prognosis.

top_papers.title: Multiple isozymes of heparan sulfate/heparin GlcNAc N-deacetylase/GlcN N-sulfotransferase. Structure and activity of the fourth member, NDST4.
top_papers.key_finding: Cloned and characterized NDST4, showing it as the fourth member of the NDST family with distinct enzymatic properties and restricted tissue expression compared to other NDSTs.

top_papers.title: Characterization of heparan sulfate N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase isoform 4 using synthetic oligosaccharide substrates.
top_papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
top_papers.key_finding: Characterized recombinant NDST4 enzyme activity, showing it lacks N-deacetylase activity but has N-sulfotransferase activity, suggesting NDST4 alone may not regulate heparan sulfate domain distribution effectively in vivo.

top_papers.title: Regulated translation of heparan sulfate N-acetylglucosamine N-deacetylase/n-sulfotransferase isozymes by structured 5'-untranslated regions and internal ribosome entry sites.
top_papers.key_finding: Studied the 5'-UTR sequences of NDST4 and other NDST isozymes, revealing complex translational regulation including internal ribosome entry sites that modulate NDST4 expression.

top_papers.title: A pseudoautosomal glycosylation disorder prompts the revision of dolichol biosynthesis.
top_papers.key_finding: This study identifies DHRSX as a critical enzyme in dolichol biosynthesis, performing the first and third steps in a three-step pathway, and reports a pseudoautosomal-recessive congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by missense variants in DHRSX.

top_papers.title: Absence of the dolichol synthesis gene DHRSX leads to N-glycosylation defects in Lec5 and Lec9 Chinese hamster ovary cells.
top_papers.key_finding: Demonstrates that absence of DHRSX leads to N-glycosylation defects in Chinese hamster ovary cells, confirming DHRSX's role in dolichol synthesis and glycosylation processes through functional complementation experiments.

top_papers.title: DHRSX, a novel non-classical secretory protein associated with starvation induced autophagy.
top_papers.key_finding: Identifies DHRSX as a novel non-classical secretory protein that promotes starvation-induced autophagy, with functional evidence from overexpression and knockdown experiments in human cell lines.

top_papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing identifies new candidate genes for nonobstructive azoospermia.
top_papers.key_finding: DHRSX is listed among genes with potential single nucleotide variants associated with nonobstructive azoospermia, suggesting a possible link to infertility though without detailed functional analysis.

top_papers.title: Xp22.33 Duplication Encompassing PAR1 in a Male with Syndromic Neurodevelopmental Disorder and Tall Stature.
top_papers.key_finding: DHRSX is included among genes duplicated in Xp22.33 region in a patient with neurodevelopmental disorder, but the paper does not specifically study DHRSX function or biology.

top_papers.title: Memory, mood and associated neuroanatomy in individuals with steroid sulphatase deficiency (X-linked ichthyosis).
top_papers.key_finding: This study investigates the consequences of constitutive STS gene deficiency on memory and mood in humans with X-linked ichthyosis, showing poorer memory performance and altered neuroanatomy associated with STS deletions.

top_papers.title: New structural insights provide a different angle on steroid sulfatase action.
top_papers.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
top_papers.key_finding: Provides new structural insights into the steroid sulfatase (STS) enzyme, challenging previous views of its membrane topology and suggesting a trimeric membrane-associated complex with implications for its enzymatic regulation.

top_papers.title: Cardiac arrhythmia, developmental delay, epilepsy and ichthyosis due to Xp22.31 deletion: review of literature and case report.
top_papers.key_finding: Reviews clinical manifestations including ichthyosis linked to Xp22.31 deletions encompassing the STS gene, highlighting neurological and cardiac phenotypes in patients with hemizygous deletions affecting STS.

top_papers.title: Genotype-driven sensitivity of mice to tick-borne encephalitis virus correlates with differential host responses in peripheral macrophages and brain.
top_papers.key_finding: Uses STS mouse strain to study differential host responses to tick-borne encephalitis virus, indicating genetic contributions of the STS genome region to viral resistance and immune responses.

top_papers.title: Haemophilia B, severe childhood obesity and other extra-haematological features associated with similar 4Mb-deletions on Xq27: Clinical findings, molecular insights and literature update.
top_papers.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
top_papers.key_finding: Reports on large Xq27 deletions including the F9 gene and proximate genes; although STS is not the main focus, the study involves genotype-phenotype correlations in X-linked deletions that may be relevant to STS genomic context.

top_papers.title: Multivariate eQTL mapping uncovers functional variation on the X-chromosome associated with complex disease traits.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified a strong eSNP (rs35975601) associated with F8A1 gene expression on the X-chromosome, linking it to type 1 diabetes risk variants, demonstrating functional genetic variation affecting F8A1 expression.

top_papers.title: PCR assay for the inversion causing severe Hemophilia A and its application.
top_papers.key_finding: Developed a PCR assay targeting F8A1 and related gene regions to detect gene inversion causing severe Hemophilia A, enabling discrimination between carriers and wild type with high sensitivity and specificity.

top_papers.title: Identification of Full-Length Wild-Type and Mutant Huntingtin Interacting Proteins by Crosslinking Immunoprecipitation in Mice Brain Cortex.
top_papers.key_finding: F8A1/HAP40 protein was identified as an interactor of both wild-type and mutant huntingtin protein in mouse brain cortex, suggesting a role in Huntington's disease pathology related to vesicle transport and exocytosis.

top_papers.title: Development and characterization of a specific IgG monoclonal antibody toward the Lewis x antigen using splenocytes of Schistosoma mansoni-infected mice.
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions an antibody named F8A1.1 targeting Lewis x antigen, but this is unrelated to the F8A1 gene; the paper focuses on immunology of Schistosoma mansoni infection.

top_papers.title: Comprehensive evaluation of the PCDHB family in gastric cancer: Prognostic significance, immune infiltration, and experimental validation of PCDHB5's oncogenic role.
top_papers.key_finding: This study directly investigates PCDHB5's oncogenic role in gastric cancer, demonstrating its upregulation, mutation patterns, correlation with immune infiltration, and prognostic significance, supported by multi-omics data and experimental validation.

top_papers.title: Weighted genes associated with the progression of retinoblastoma: Evidence from bioinformatic analysis.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 is included among protocadherin beta family genes associated with retinoblastoma progression, identified via bioinformatic analysis and gene co-expression networks, suggesting a role in tumor biology.

top_papers.title: Long noncoding RNA HOTAIR promotes metastasis of renal cell carcinoma by up-regulating histone H3K27 demethylase JMJD3.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 expression is regulated epigenetically in renal cell carcinoma metastasis, with HOTAIR knockdown increasing PCDHB5 levels, indicating a role in chromatin state and cancer progression.

top_papers.title: Nine differentially expressed genes from a post mortem study and their association with suicidal status in a sample of suicide completers, attempters and controls.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 was one of nine differentially expressed genes studied for association with suicidal behavior, with nominal but not statistically robust genetic associations reported.

top_papers.title: Influence of differentially expressed genes from suicide post-mortem study on personality traits as endophenotypes on healthy subjects and suicide attempters.
top_papers.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 SNPs were analyzed for influence on personality traits as endophenotypes related to suicide, showing some modulation but without strong conclusive evidence.

research_themes: lysosomal function and ion channel interactions

top_papers.title: Variants in the zinc transporter TMEM163 cause a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
top_papers.key_finding: Variants in TMEM163 cause hypomyelinating leukodystrophy characterized by impaired zinc efflux function, reduced myelin gene expression, and oligodendrocyte dysfunction.

top_papers.title: Functional Study of
top_papers.key_finding: De novo TMEM163 variants identified in hypomyelinating leukodystrophy patients alter zinc efflux activity and cause myelin deficits and locomotor disability in zebrafish models.

top_papers.title: The role of TMEM163 protein in thyroid microcarcinoma: expression pattern and clinical implications.
top_papers.key_finding: TMEM163 is overexpressed in thyroid microcarcinoma and modulates proliferation, migration, and invasion of cancer cells, suggesting a regulatory role in tumor biology.

top_papers.title: Elevated vesicular Zn2+ in dorsal root ganglion neurons expressing the transporter TMEM163 causes age-associated itchy skin in mice.
top_papers.key_finding: TMEM163 expression and vesicular Zn2+ levels increase in dorsal root ganglion neurons with aging, causing chronic itch via inhibition of spinal NPY+ interneurons.

top_papers.title: A zinc transporter, transmembrane protein 163, is critical for the biogenesis of platelet dense granules.
top_papers.key_finding: TMEM163 is identified as a critical zinc transporter necessary for platelet dense granule biogenesis, with reduced expression in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome models and patients.

top_papers.title: Protocadherin alpha 3 inhibits lung squamous cell carcinoma metastasis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHA3 is low expressed in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) cell lines, and its overexpression significantly impairs LUSC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, indicating that PCDHA3 inhibits LUSC metastasis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

top_papers.title: Novel ultra-rare exonic variants identified in a founder population implicate cadherins in schizophrenia.
top_papers.key_finding: A recurrent missense mutation in PCDHA3 was identified in schizophrenia cases, resulting in cytoplasmic aggregates and failure of homophilic interactions on the plasma membrane, implicating PCDHA3 and cadherin family genes in schizophrenia risk.

top_papers.title: Protocadherin alpha gene cluster variants are potentially associated with short root anomaly in Japanese.
top_papers.key_finding: Four missense variants in the protocadherin alpha gene cluster including PCDHA3 were identified in Japanese patients with short root anomaly, suggesting a genetic association of PCDHA3 variants with this dental phenotype.

top_papers.title: LncRNA-ZXF1 stabilizes P21 expression in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma by inhibiting ubiquitination-mediated degradation and regulating the miR-378a-3p/PCDHA3 axis.
top_papers.key_finding: LncRNA-ZXF1 regulates endometrioid endometrial carcinoma cell proliferation and invasion partly by modulating PCDHA3 expression through a miR-378a-3p/PCDHA3 axis, suggesting a role of PCDHA3 in tumor suppression mechanisms.

top_papers.title: A risk scoring model for lung squamous cell carcinoma based on epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related genes: an integrative analysis of prognosis and immune infiltration characteristics.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHA3 was included in a six-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related prognostic signature for lung squamous cell carcinoma, indicating its potential relevance in cancer prognosis though the study context differs from the research question.

top_papers.title: Celecoxib Enhances Oxidative Muscle Fibre Formation and Improves Muscle Functions Through Prokr1 Activation in Mice.
top_papers.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
top_papers.key_finding: Celecoxib acts as a PROKR1 agonist and improves muscle functions by enhancing oxidative muscle fiber formation through PROKR1 activation in mice, suggesting PROKR1 as a therapeutic target for muscular disorders.

top_papers.title: Prokineticin receptor 1 ameliorates insulin resistance in skeletal muscle.
top_papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
top_papers.key_finding: PROKR1 improves insulin resistance in skeletal muscle by activating PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling pathways and promoting GLUT4 translocation, indicating a direct metabolic role of PROKR1 in muscle cells.

top_papers.title: MRAP2a Binds and Modulates Activity and Localisation of Prokineticin Receptor 1 in Zebrafish.
top_papers.key_finding: MRAP2a binds to zebrafish PROKR1 and modulates its activity and localization, demonstrating regulatory interactions that affect PROKR1 signaling in energy homeostasis.

top_papers.title: Regions of MRAP2 required for the inhibition of orexin and prokineticin receptor signaling.
top_papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
top_papers.key_finding: MRAP2 regulates the trafficking and signaling of PROKR1 and orexin receptor 1, identifying specific MRAP2 regions involved in modulating PROKR1 activity relevant to energy homeostasis control.

top_papers.title: Prokineticin receptor 1 as a novel suppressor of preadipocyte proliferation and differentiation to control obesity.
top_papers.key_finding: PROKR1 acts as a suppressor of preadipocyte proliferation and differentiation, controlling adipose tissue expansion and obesity development in mouse models.

top_papers.title: Application of a risk score model based on tyrosine-related genes in the prognosis and treatment of patients with lung adenocarcinoma.
top_papers.key_finding: This study identified ZFP3 as one of seven tyrosine-related genes forming a risk score model for diagnosis and prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting its potential role as a biomarker and its impact on immunotherapy efficacy and drug sensitivity.

top_papers.title: Prediction of Patients With High-Risk Osteosarcoma on the Basis of XGBoost Algorithm Using Transcriptome and Methylation Data From SGH-OS Cohort.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 was included among nine genes used in an XGBoost-based classifier to predict high-risk osteosarcoma subtypes, indicating its potential involvement in osteosarcoma molecular characteristics though the study does not focus on ZFP3 biology.

top_papers.title: An eleven gene molecular signature for extra-capsular spread in oral squamous cell carcinoma serves as a prognosticator of outcome in patients without nodal metastases.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 was part of an 11-gene molecular signature associated with extracapsular spread in oral squamous cell carcinoma, serving as a prognosticator of outcome in patients without nodal metastases.

top_papers.title: The predictive value of plasma exosomal lncRNAs/mRNAs in NSCLC patients receiving immunotherapy.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper mentions lnc-ZFP3-3 as a long non-coding RNA trans-regulating certain mRNAs in non-small cell lung cancer patients but does not directly study the ZFP3 gene itself.

top_papers.title: Chromosomal localization of two human zinc finger protein genes, ZNF24 (KOX17) and ZNF29 (KOX26), to 18q12 and 17p13-p12, respectively.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 is mentioned in the context of chromosomal localization studies, suggesting a zinc finger gene complex on human chromosome 17p, but the study does not investigate ZFP3 function or biology.

top_papers.title: Association Between Circulating Gremlin 2 and β-Cell Function Among Participants With Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.
top_papers.key_finding: Circulating Gremlin 2 (Grem2) levels are associated with β-cell function in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, with levels restored after antidiabetic treatment, suggesting a role of GREM2 in diabetes pathophysiology.

top_papers.title: BMP Antagonist Gremlin 2 Regulates Hippocampal Neurogenesis and Is Associated with Seizure Susceptibility and Anxiety.
top_papers.key_finding: GREM2 acts as a potent BMP antagonist regulating hippocampal neurogenesis, and its deficiency in mice is associated with seizure susceptibility and anxiety, highlighting its role in neural progenitor cell function.

top_papers.title: GREM2 is associated with human central obesity and inhibits visceral preadipocyte browning.
top_papers.key_finding: GREM2 is associated with human central obesity and inhibits visceral preadipocyte browning, with elevated circulating GREM2 levels correlating with visceral fat volume and functional studies showing Grem2 suppresses browning in adipose tissue.

top_papers.title: Deletion of Gremlin-2 alters estrous cyclicity and disrupts female fertility in mice†.
top_papers.key_finding: Deletion of GREM2 in mice alters estrous cyclicity and reduces female fertility, linked to decreased ovarian AMH production, indicating GREM2's important role in female reproductive physiology.

top_papers.title: GREM2 nucleotide variants and the risk of tooth agenesis.
top_papers.key_finding: The functional GREM2 mutation p.Gln76Glu is associated with tooth agenesis and dental anomalies in patients, supporting GREM2's involvement in dental development and pathology.

top_papers.title: Schizophrenia-associated changes in neuronal subpopulations in the human midbrain.
top_papers.key_finding: Single nucleus RNA-sequencing identified neuronal populations in human midbrain expressing SLC17A6 (VGLUT2), revealing schizophrenia-associated changes in these glutamatergic neurons.

top_papers.title: Parkinson's disease-associated, sex-specific changes in DNA methylation at PARK7 (DJ-1), SLC17A6 (VGLUT2), PTPRN2 (IA-2β), and NR4A2 (NURR1) in cortical neurons.
top_papers.key_finding: This study reports sex-specific Parkinson's disease-associated DNA methylation changes in SLC17A6 (VGLUT2) in cortical neurons, linking epigenetic regulation of SLC17A6 to PD pathogenesis.

top_papers.title: KDM6B cooperates with Tau and regulates synaptic plasticity and cognition via inducing VGLUT1/2.
top_papers.key_finding: KDM6B epigenetically regulates synaptic plasticity and cognition by inducing expression of SLC17A6 (VGLUT2), demonstrating a mechanism of glutamate transporter regulation in neurons.

top_papers.title: Efficient Mass Spectral Analysis of Active Transporters Overexpressed in Escherichia coli.
top_papers.key_finding: Developed a method for mass spectral analysis of purified active SLC17A6 (VGLUT2) protein overexpressed in E. coli, confirming its glutamate transport activity and enabling structural studies.

top_papers.title: Reduced gene expression levels of Munc13-1 and additional components of the presynaptic exocytosis machinery upon conditional targeting of Vglut2 in the adolescent mouse.
top_papers.key_finding: Conditional targeting of SLC17A6 (Vglut2) in adolescent mouse brain leads to reduced expression of presynaptic exocytosis machinery components, linking SLC17A6 to synaptic function and behavior.

top_papers.title: Elevated SAMD3 expression in T cells predicts improved survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients.
top_papers.key_finding: Elevated SAMD3 expression in cytotoxic CD8 T cells predicts improved survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients, highlighting SAMD3 as a biomarker of T cell function with potential for precision immunotherapy.

top_papers.title: Identification and validation of poor prognosis immunoevasive subtype of esophageal cancer with tumor-infiltrating SAMD3 + NK cell abundance.
top_papers.key_finding: SAMD3 expression in tumor-infiltrating NK cells correlates with poor prognosis in esophageal cancer; knockdown of SAMD3 enhances NK cell antitumor activity and reduces tumor growth in xenograft models, indicating SAMD3 as a critical modulator of NK cell function.

top_papers.title: Multi-Omics Characterization of Early- and Adult-Onset Major Depressive Disorder.
top_papers.key_finding: A significant genetic variant within an intron of SAMD3 was associated with age at onset of major depressive disorder, with gene expression enrichment in brain and embryonic development, suggesting a role for SAMD3 in MDD susceptibility.

top_papers.title: Retinoic acid and androgen receptors combine to achieve tissue specific control of human prostatic transglutaminase expression: a novel regulatory network with broader significance.
top_papers.key_finding: SAMD3 is among genes regulated by retinoic acid receptor and androgen receptor in human prostate, indicating its involvement in tissue-specific gene regulation networks.

top_papers.title: MicroRNA expression abnormalities in limited cutaneous scleroderma and diffuse cutaneous scleroderma.
top_papers.key_finding: SAMD3 is a predicted target gene regulated by dysregulated microRNAs in scleroderma, implicating it in fibrosis-related pathophysiology.

top_papers.title: Genetic Markers of Spina Bifida: Enrichment of Pathogenic Variants and Variants of Uncertain Significance.

top_papers.title: Anti-tumor potential of high salt in breast Cancer cell lines.

top_papers.title: Comprehensive CRISPR-Cas9 screens identify genetic determinants of drug responsiveness in multiple myeloma.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper identifies PCDHA5 as one of the structural genes linked to drug resistance in multiple myeloma through CRISPR-Cas9 screens, indicating a functional impact of PCDHA5 mutations on drug responsiveness.

top_papers.title: Maternal immune activation downregulates schizophrenia genes in the foetal mouse brain.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHA5 is not specifically discussed; the paper focuses on schizophrenia genes broadly without detailed analysis of PCDHA5.

top_papers.title: Predicting the Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma Diagnosis and Prognosis Markers by Unique DNA Methylation and Gene Expression Profiles.
